studies.title: Structure of the nutrient-sensing hub GATOR2
studies.finding: Cryo-EM structure of human GATOR2: a 1.1 MDa, two-fold symmetric cage built on an octagonal scaffold decorated with eight pairs of WD40 beta-propellers, and a map of where Sestrin2 and CASTOR1 dock. It substantially advances the GATOR2 side of the sensor module, though how GATOR2 inhibits GATOR1 is still not fully settled.

studies.finding: The authors made knock-in mice in which all five phosphorylatable serines of ribosomal protein S6 were replaced by alanine, so rpS6 could not be phosphorylated. Contrary to the then widely accepted model, translational control of 5'TOP mRNAs was unaffected. studies.finding: Isolated mTOR as the FKBP12-rapamycin-associated protein controlling G1-S progression.

studies.title: Rac1 regulates the activity of mTORC1 and mTORC2 and controls cellular size
studies.finding: Rac1 binds and regulates both mTORC1 and mTORC2, controlling their localization and cell growth.

studies.title: The Rag GTPases bind raptor and mediate amino acid signaling to mTORC1
studies.finding: Identifies the Rag GTPase family as the missing link that lets mTORC1 sense amino acids by controlling whether mTOR is positioned near its activator Rheb.

studies.title: PRAS40 is an insulin-regulated inhibitor of the mTORC1 protein kinase
studies.finding: Identified PRAS40 as the missing insulin-controlled brake INSIDE mTORC1. When insulin is absent PRAS40 clamps the complex shut; insulin makes Akt phosphorylate PRAS40, releasing the brake so Rheb can fully switch mTORC1 on. Explained how hormone signals set the exact strength of mTORC1 activity.

studies.title: "Trojan" Methionine Probe Reveals PKM2 as a Methionine-Sensing Protein in the mTORC1 Pathway
studies.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
studies.finding: Identifies PKM2 as a direct methionine sensor for mTORC1. A photoaffinity methionine analogue plus chemoproteomics showed that PKM2 binds free methionine through a distinct recognition pocket — independently of its glycolytic enzyme activity — and transduces methionine availability to mTORC1 via the GATOR2 complex. studies.finding: A lysosome-to-nucleus mechanism uses mTOR-dependent TFEB phosphorylation to sense lysosomal state.

studies.title: A gene network regulating lysosomal biogenesis and function
studies.finding: The authors found that most lysosomal genes show coordinated expression and share a promoter motif (later called the CLEAR element) that is bound and regulated by the transcription factor TFEB. Under conditions of abnormal lysosomal storage, TFEB moved from the cytoplasm to the nucleus and switched on its target genes. studies.title: The Bi-steric, mTORC1-Selective Inhibitor, RMC-5552, in Advanced Solid Tumors: A Phase 1 Trial
studies.finding: First-in-human, open-label dose-escalation trial (n=57, advanced solid tumors, no comparator arm) of a bi-steric mTORC1-selective inhibitor. Treatment-related hyperglycemia was low (4%) and not dose-limiting, alongside a 64% disease control rate. studies.title: Mammalian target of rapamycin signaling in cardiac physiology and disease
studies.finding: Review of mTOR signalling in cardiac physiology and disease.

studies.title: Structure of mammalian AMPK and its regulation by ADP
studies.finding: AMP binding to the gamma regulatory domain promotes phosphorylation of AMPK and protects it from dephosphorylation. ADP binding to one site also protects against dephosphorylation but does not activate allosterically. Crystal structure of an active AMPK complex.

studies.title: Ribosomal protein S6 kinase 1 signaling regulates mammalian life span
studies.finding: Deleting S6K1 (a direct mTORC1 effector) extended lifespan in FEMALE mice (+19% median); the effect was not significant in males. It also protected against age-related bone, immune and motor decline. One of the clearest cases of the sex dimorphism catalogued in gap H6 - and a reminder that a single downstream branch, not mTORC1 as a whole, can carry much of the ageing signal.

studies.title: A lysosome-to-nucleus signalling mechanism senses and regulates the lysosome via mTOR and TFEB
studies.finding: A lysosome-to-nucleus mechanism uses mTOR-dependent TFEB phosphorylation to sense lysosomal state.

studies.title: TFEB links autophagy to lysosomal biogenesis
studies.finding: Showed that TFEB drives a coordinated autophagy and lysosomal gene programme during starvation. In this paper TFEB was regulated by ERK2 phosphorylation; its control by mTORC1 at the lysosome was established in later work (SET2012).

studies.title: TFEB controls cellular lipid metabolism through a starvation-induced autoregulatory loop
studies.finding: The authors found that fasting switches on the TFEB gene in mouse liver, muscle and kidney, and that TFEB drives its own transcription by binding CLEAR sites in its promoter, an autoregulatory loop that starvation strengthens. studies.title: Inappropriate activation of the TSC/Rheb/mTOR/S6K cassette induces IRS1/2 depletion, insulin resistance, and cell survival deficiencies
studies.finding: The companion paper to Harrington 2004, published two months later. In cultured mammalian cells, constitutive Rheb/mTOR/S6K activity depletes IRS1 and IRS2, producing cellular insulin resistance and impaired survival signalling. Together the two papers establish the S6K1 -> IRS negative feedback arm.

studies.title: The tumor suppressor LKB1 kinase directly activates AMP-activated kinase and regulates apoptosis in response to energy stress
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
studies.finding: The paper that identified LKB1 as the upstream kinase for AMPK: LKB1 directly phosphorylates AMPK-alpha on Thr172, and LKB1-null cells cannot activate AMPK under energy stress. This is the canonical source for the LKB1 -> AMPK step that gates the whole energy-sensing arm upstream of mTORC1.

studies.title: The LKB1 tumor suppressor negatively regulates mTOR signaling
studies.finding: Reported that LKB1 is needed to switch mTOR signalling off when cellular ATP falls, and that this requires AMPK and TSC2. Lkb1-null fibroblasts and the hamartomatous gut polyps of Lkb1 mutant mice showed raised signalling downstream of mTOR. studies.finding: Mice with the S6K1 gene disrupted were viable and fertile but smaller, with the growth effect strongest during embryonic development. studies.title: Lysosomal GPCR-like protein LYCHOS signals cholesterol sufficiency to mTORC1
studies.finding: Identifies LYCHOS (previously annotated GPR155) as a lysosomal cholesterol sensor for mTORC1. Cholesterol binds the amino-terminal permease-like region; mutating that site impairs mTORC1 activation. At high cholesterol LYCHOS binds GATOR1 through a conserved cytoplasm-facing loop, and by sequestering GATOR1 it promotes cholesterol- and Rag-dependent recruitment of mTORC1 to the lysosome. studies.finding: LncRNA DLX6-AS1 activates PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling to promote necroptosis in myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury; inhibiting DLX6-AS1 suppresses necroptosis and protects cardiomyocytes.

studies.title: Redox activation of ATG5 licenses autophagy upon nutrient restriction
studies.finding: Dietary restriction selectively oxidizes a specific, tissue-resolved set of cysteines rather than oxidizing the proteome broadly. One of the most strongly oxidized is Cys19 on the core autophagy protein ATG5; this oxidation is required for ATG5 to bind ATG10 and form the ATG5-ATG12 conjugate that lipidates LC3B and builds the autophagosome. studies.title: D-Amino Acid Prodrug DLMEH Activates mTORC1 via Sestrin2 to Restore Muscle Protein Synthesis in Sarcopenia.
studies.finding: DLMEH, a D-leucine ester prodrug, binds Sestrin2 with leucine-like potency (Kd 28.3 uM, equivalent to L-leucine) and activates mTORC1 in a Sestrin2-dependent way. It restored protein synthesis in human myotubes and preserved muscle mass, grip strength and endurance in a rat dexamethasone-induced atrophy model (not an ageing sarcopenia model).

studies.finding: In 46 term placentas, male placentas showed higher mTORC1 signalling (increased S6RP phosphorylation, reduced 4E-BP1), greater System A amino acid transport and higher mitochondrial respiratory capacity than female placentas, and male pregnancies had a higher birth-weight-to-placental-weight ratio. studies.finding: In middle-aged marmosets given daily rapamycin, 9 months of treatment produced only minor changes in cellular blood counts, so hematological side effects are not likely outcomes of long-term rapamycin in relatively healthy middle-aged animals. studies.title: Enforcing mTORC1 activity in therapeutic CD4+ T cells promotes persistence but eventual immune exhaustion
studies.finding: Enforced RHEB overexpression (mTORC1 hyperactivation) in therapeutic CD4+ T cells boosts initial proliferation/persistence after adoptive transfer, but drives cells toward an exhausted phenotype (co-inhibitory receptors, impaired re-proliferation on rechallenge) -- a double-edged sword for CAR/TCR-T cell engineering, distinct from the CD8 response to the same manipulation.

studies.title: Control of amino-acid transport by antigen receptors coordinates the metabolic reprogramming essential for T cell differentiation
studies.finding: Antigen-receptor-driven System-L (SLC7A5) amino-acid transport controls mTORC1 and T-cell differentiation.

studies.finding: In a rigorous randomized crossover trial, 63 healthy adults completed both a normal-protein (20% energy) and a reduced-protein (10% energy) diet for 4 weeks each. Despite preclinical evidence that dietary protein restriction should activate autophagy via mTORC1 inhibition, directly measured autophagic flux in blood immune cells did not change between the two diets. studies.finding: Lifespan and cardiometabolic health were determined not by caloric intake but by the protein:carbohydrate ratio; a low protein ratio was associated with lower hepatic mTOR activation.

studies.title: Urolithin A activates mitophagy via the AMPK-mTOR axis and modulates the gut-ceramide axis to ameliorate cardiac remodeling in HFpEF
studies.finding: Urolithin A ameliorates HFpEF cardiac remodeling in mice by activating AMPK and inhibiting mTOR to restore mitophagic flux, while simultaneously remodeling the gut microbiome-ceramide axis to reduce lipotoxic stress.

studies.title: Continuous sensing of nutrients and growth factors by the mTORC1-TFEB axis
studies.finding: Live imaging of single MCF10A cells shows mTORC1-TFEB signalling adjusts continuously to amino acids and insulin, given alone, one after another or together; at physiological amino acid levels TFEB, AMPK and AKT activity fluctuate in step, and these graded changes track protein synthesis rate through a distributed set of mTORC1 effectors.

studies.title: Inhibition of mTOR by rapamycin abolishes cognitive deficits and reduces amyloid-beta levels in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease
studies.finding: Connected the longevity drug to a specific age-related disease. Long-term rapamycin prevented memory deficits and lowered toxic amyloid-beta in an Alzheimer's mouse model - and the benefit tracked with INCREASED autophagy in neurons. Suggested that the same autophagy boost that may slow aging could also help clear disease-causing proteins.

studies.title: Nutrient/TOR signaling controls adipose mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM) to regulate organismal growth in Drosophila
studies.finding: In Drosophila larvae, nutrient/TOR signaling in the fat body (a key nutrient-sensing tissue) post-transcriptionally suppresses the mitochondrial transcription factor TFAM, and this TOR→TFAM axis in fat-body tissue controls whole-body developmental growth — a mechanistic link between nutrient sensing and interorgan growth control via mitochondrial bioenergetics.

studies.title: PDCD4 inhibits translation initiation by binding to eIF4A using both its MA3 domains
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
studies.finding: Both MA3 domains of PDCD4 bind the N-terminal domain of eIF4A and compete with eIF4G and RNA for it, which explains how PDCD4 blocks translation initiation.

studies.title: Medulloblastoma-associated mutations in the RNA helicase DDX3X/DED1 cause defects in the translational response to TORC1 inhibition
studies.finding: Medulloblastoma-associated DDX3X mutations, modeled in the yeast ortholog Ded1 (ded1-mam), cause rapamycin-resistant growth and selectively upregulate translation of unstructured-5'UTR pro-growth transcripts after TORC1 inhibition, a mechanism by which mutant DDX3X may let tumor cells bypass TORC1-dependent stress/growth control.

studies.title: Targeting mTOR restores tau-induced metabolic, mitochondrial, and cognitive deficits in a tauopathy mouse model
studies.finding: In mice engineered to overexpress a phosphomimetic tau variant, one week of rapamycin partially mitigated tau-driven mitochondrial dysfunction and cognitive impairment in the Morris water maze - extends the mTOR-autophagy-neurodegeneration link (already seen with Huntington's) to a direct tau-phosphorylation mechanism relevant to Alzheimer's.
